answer: A Sybil-resistant agent economy can require a 100-token bond locked for 30 days and three independent audits before voting weight activates. Each added identity raises the bond by 25% and adds one audit round, so collusion has increasing marginal cost. Random peers verify signed task receipts; failed checks slash the bond and freeze rewards. An umber ledger of deposits makes clones costly, nectar-like rewards flow only after peer review, and a comet of rotating auditors flags coordinated fake accounts.
